messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High error rate detected on gateway-prod (5xx/timeouts). P50 latency rising; paging on-call. Links: https://redwood.monitoring/alerts/4821 :rotating_light:

alex.s: Paging in. seeing ~30% 5xx across /v1/generate, lots of 504s. Customers reporting streaming interruptions.

maya: confirming spikes in scheduler queue length, one batching pool showing sustained queue backlog (~12k). head-of-line blocking symptoms.

sean: logs show many long-running KV-cache loads during batch assembly, some requests stuck in prepare step for >3s. sample: ```ERROR scheduler.go:245 prepareBatch timeout waiting for kv-resolve (key=project:12345)```

priya: Gateway showing upstream timeouts to runtime instances, 502/504. TL;DR: batches not draining, gateway waits -> times out.

alex.s: Quick customer impact note: Affected endpoints are stream + chat flows. Some sessions get truncated mid-stream. We're seeing elevated retries from clients.

oncall-bot: @alex.s assigned (on-call). Escalation to pagerduty already sent.

alex.s: Taking. immediate plan: 1) redirect new traffic away from saturated scheduler pool 2) enable emergency backpressure routing to dedicated low-latency pool 3) kick off KV-load eviction on hot workers 4) assess need for temporary throttle on noisy clients.

maya: Agree. I can run an emergency route update to move traffic for model-rank A -> pool-b. pool-b has free capacity and smaller batches.

sean: On KV side, there's a runaway write that keeps locks open (suspect tenant replay). I can push a config to lower kv-load TTL and evict entries older than 5m. Command: ```rctl kv evict --pool scheduler-7 --age 300s --dry-run=false```

priya: If we evict aggressively we might see cold-start latency on some requests but that beats 504s. prioritize latency-sensitive routes for fallback.

alex.s: Doing route switch now: ```redwood route update --from scheduler-7 --to pool-b --match '/v1/generate' --throttle 0.6``` will ramp to 60% then 100% in 30s.

ops-engineer: Started KV eviction job; progress 30% after 40s. Observing a slight drop in batch assembly time already.

maya: Route update at 60% -> hit threshold OK. Increasing to 100% now.

sean: Seeing influx to pool-b, instance CPU going up but latency improving. 5xx rate dropping from 30% -> 8% in ~90s.

alex.s: Good. Marking initial mitigation success. Next: figure root cause for scheduler backlog. Any recent deploys?

priya: No deploys in last 2 hours. Telemetry shows a single client (api-key: cli-zzz) generated huge fanout requests with large context sizes; their request tokens doubled expected distribution -> oversized batches and long KV resolves.

sean: I’m pulling sample traces. Looks like a malformed prompt loop causing repeated streaming reconnects from that client. Will reach out to SE/contact owner.

maya: Safety step: enable per-client rate-limits on noisy api-key as temporary mitigation. ```redwood rate-limit update --key cli-zzz --max-req 10m```

alex.s: Applying now. Also lowering max batch size for scheduler-7 to avoid long assembly times: ```kubectl patch cm scheduler-config -p '{"data":{"max_batch_tokens":"1024"}}'```

ops-engineer: Batch size change rolled, KV eviction job finished. Scheduler queue length back to normal. Gateway 504s down to baseline.

priya: Please verify customer-facing impact and notify CS. We should open a post-incident ticket for long-term: fix prompt validation, better per-client backpressure, and KV lock visibility.

alex.s: Will draft P1 incident report. Quick customer note: Most customers auto-retried and had degraded streams; small percentage saw hard truncation — CS to contact top 5 affected.

sean: For follow-up: replicate the malformed prompt locally, add a rate-limit rule when token size > 8k, and create an alert for sudden change in token-size distribution per key.

maya: I'm leaving routing as-is for now. If anything spikes again notify and we'll failover back to pool-b or spin up dedicated instances.

oncall-bot: Handoff: alex.s -> maya at 12:34 UTC. maya is now primary on-call for remediation window.

maya: taking 1, will stay on for the next hour and coordinate mitigation work. I'll own the postmortem draft.

alex.s: thanks team — adding incident to timeline and closing live paging. I'll update the incident ticket with mitigation steps and timelines. :white_check_mark:
